name: drawing_is_a_second_document
why: THE FIRST BENCH CASE THAT REACHES THE DRAWING. Seven drawing operations had been in the catalogue for months, marked «proved», with zero declared cases. The reason was not lack of will: the bench ran every step on the SAME document, and `create_drawing` opens a second one. A case that created a drawing put the views inside the part, or more often stopped on «the active document is not a drawing» -- a right message for a problem that whoever wrote the case could not solve, so nobody wrote the case. Now the bench follows the document the operation DECLARES (`Esito.DocumentoNuovo`), never the active document of SOLIDWORKS. This case is the proof that it does.
_an_operation_without_a_case_is_not_test: It is declared. And if the bench cannot set up the situation, the case cannot be written, the operation stays still, and it looks like a matter of priority. It is the same shape as GA0 for the assemblies: there the entry had become the FIRST of all; here the entry was not there at all, and was born now (GT0).
_why_it_does_not_end_with_center_marks: The first draft of this case went as far as `center_marks`, and that is how it was discovered that this API does not work on this installation: it answers `True` and puts nothing, in twenty-five combinations, on all three views, and even selecting the circular edges one by one. The operation was set to `Provata = false` and the case stops before it. **What this case proves -- that the bench knows how to turn the page -- is true all the same**, and must not be thrown away together with what could not be done.

expect.why: 120 x 80 x 10. If this does not add up, all the rest of the case measures a part that is not the one I believe.

expect.tolerance_why: the diameter is read from CylinderParams, not from the argument
as above. Two holes, two diameters: the second cut did not eat the first.

96000 minus three times pi*5^2*10 = 2356.19, so 93643.81. The volume is the only measure that says the holes are really THROUGH and not blind: a blind hole would have the same diameter and a different volume.
expect._the_first_number_i_had_written_was_9364: Wrong by 0.45 -- a mistake of mine in arithmetic, not of the part. It had passed all the same because the tolerance was 0.5, that is **wide enough to cover my mistake**: it is exactly the way a generous tolerance stops measuring. Measured 93643.806. Now the tolerance is 0.1 and the number is the true one.

expect.why: A VIEW ATTACHES TO THE PATH OF THE PART, not to the document in memory: a part never saved cannot be put on a drawing, and it is the reason the case needs this step.

saved without warnings. That the file EXISTS is already guaranteed by the operation, which refuses if «File.Exists» says no after the save: here we look that SOLIDWORKS had nothing to object to -- a warning on a save is almost always a reference that was not found.

**THIS IS THE EXPECTATION THAT PROVES GT0, and it is the whole case in one line.** The state the bench re-reads after the step must be that of the DRAWING, no longer that of the part. If the bench did not follow the declared document, here it would say «part» -- and all the steps after would measure the part believing they measure the drawing.
the drawing must have been BORN FROM THIS PART, not from another document left open from a previous run
expect._without_extension_and_not_out_of_lazine: The first draft asked for «...sldprt» and turned red: **the same file is written in two ways depending on who reports it.** `save_document` sends back the path AS IT WAS ASKED (lower case, because I wrote it in the case); `create_drawing` reads it from `GetPathName()`, and SOLIDWORKS returns it with the extension in UPPER CASE. Neither of the two lies, and the substring operator `contiene` is case-sensitive -- rightly, because elsewhere it is needed. We compare the stem of the name, which is the thing the case really wants to say.

expect.why: one sheet: if two were born, the count of the views at the next step would be of something else

steps._and_the_part_is_named_explicitly: Added on 18/9/2026. This case was green **by luck of the draw**: it counted the views and the projection angle, not which part they came from. With another part open it would have been green all the same on a wrong drawing — *a proof that counts the objects and does not look at what they are of is green even when the part is another one.*

expect.why: **AND NOW WE ALSO LOOK AT WHAT THE VIEWS ARE OF.** It is the line that was missing from all three drawing checks: they counted three views and never asked of which part. On 18/9 a drawing came out of the wrong part and none of them noticed.
Italy draws in first angle projection, and the twin `Create3rdAngleViews2` never fails: it produces a drawing with right and left swapped that no volume measure would see
three standard views. The exact number and not «greater than zero»: a drawing with a single view has succeeded for the API and is useless for whoever cuts.

**THE TWO READINGS AGREE.** The operation says «three created»; the state starts over and re-reads the sheet view by view. Two independent roads to the same number -- if they diverged, one of the two would be lying and we would not know which. It is the same proof GA5 does on `assembly_constrained`.

**IT WAS 0, AND IT WAS THE COUNTER THAT LIED** (26/9/2026, entry W2.11). The views are born WITH the marks on the three holes: SOLIDWORKS puts them at the creation of the view (document option «centre marks on holes», switched on here), and they can be seen in the PNG. `IView.GetCenterMarkCount()` answered 0 because it does not count those; enumerating them (`GetFirstCenterMark`/`GetNext`) there are three. For a week this line kept green a hole that was not there, and hid the true defect: the state said zero marks on a sheet that had three.
expect._and_the_field_is_new: `stato.viste[].croci_di_centro` and `state.center_marks_total` were born together with this case. They are ALWAYS written, even at zero: a field that appears only when it has an interesting value teaches nobody to look for it.
